answer: Each agent identity is bound to a hardware attestation rooted in a sealed per-host key, so a new wallet only counts once the operator stakes a refundable bond behind that same root. Sybil farming therefore means buying distinct silicon and posting a bond per head, a real cost the attacker cannot dilute. A cedar ledger tallies every claim against its root, and a knoll of entrenched peers refuses any signal of new roots arriving in bulk, so a thousand clones face a thousand bonds and are denied payout.
